AI Resume Screening & Skill Matching Engine

An end-to-end NLP pipeline parsing unstructured candidate resumes (PDF/DOCX), extracting technical skill entities, and computing cosine similarity against job descriptions with FastAPI.

Author: Ananya Verma (Senior AI/ML Researcher & Curriculum Lead)
Reviewed by Rohit Sharma
Updated: Sep 28, 2026

Problem Statement & Objectives

Modern corporate recruiting portals receive thousands of heterogeneous resumes per opening. Manual candidate screening causes severe evaluation delays, keyword-matching bias, and missed qualified candidates whose resumes use synonym terminology rather than literal exact strings.

Real-World Context:High-volume recruitment workflows at enterprise software companies, placement cells filtering candidates for specialized campus hiring drives, and automated job portal applicant pre-qualifiers.

Key Project Objectives:

  • •Build a robust file-parsing subsystem that reliably extracts plain text from varied PDF and DOCX document layouts.
  • •Implement an entity-extraction pipeline that isolates technical skills, years of experience, and degrees without relying on brittle regex alone.
  • •Vectorize candidate profiles and target job descriptions using dense text embeddings to evaluate conceptual semantic fit.
  • •Provide a high-throughput, asynchronous REST API delivering scored match rankings and missing skill gap insights.

System Architecture

The system follows a modular pipeline architecture. The Ingestion Layer ingests resumes via FastAPI multipart endpoints and extracts raw text via PyMuPDF. The NLP Engine cleans the text, tokenizes, removes stopwords, and performs custom spaCy NER to extract hard technical skills and qualifications. The Vector Matcher converts candidate text and job descriptions into high-dimensional vectors, calculating cosine similarity. Results are persisted to SQLite/PostgreSQL with candidate rank scores.

Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

Step 1: Document Parsing & Text Extraction Setup

Set up a virtual environment and configure PyMuPDF (fitz) to read raw streams from PDF uploads, handling multi-column reading order.

extractor.py
import fitz  # PyMuPDF

def extract_text_from_pdf(file_bytes: bytes) -> str:
    doc = fitz.open(stream=file_bytes, filetype="pdf")
    text_blocks = []
    for page in doc:
        text_blocks.append(page.get_text("text"))
    return "\n".join(text_blocks).strip()

Step 2: Skill Entity Matching with spaCy PhraseMatcher

Load an English spaCy model and initialize PhraseMatcher with pre-compiled technical terminology tokens to extract technology entities with zero false positives.

ner_pipeline.py
import spacy
from spacy.matcher import PhraseMatcher

nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
matcher = PhraseMatcher(nlp.vocab, attr="LOWER")

TECH_SKILLS = ["Python", "FastAPI", "Docker", "PostgreSQL", "PyTorch", "React"]
patterns = [nlp.make_doc(skill) for skill in TECH_SKILLS]
matcher.add("TECH_SKILLS", patterns)

def extract_skills(text: str) -> list[str]:
    doc = nlp(text)
    matches = matcher(doc)
    return sorted(list({doc[start:end].text for _, start, end in matches}))

Step 3: Vector Similarity Engine & FastAPI Endpoint

Implement cosine similarity computation using scikit-learn's TfidfVectorizer or sentence-transformers, exposed through an asynchronous FastAPI route.

main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, File
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

app = FastAPI(title="Resume Screening Engine")

@app.post("/api/v1/score")
async def calculate_score(resume_text: str, job_text: str):
    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(stop_words="english")
    tfidf_matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform([resume_text, job_text])
    similarity = cosine_similarity(tfidf_matrix[0:1], tfidf_matrix[1:2])[0][0]
    return {"match_score": round(float(similarity) * 100, 2)}

Placement Viva & Technical Questions

Questions commonly asked by college examiners and product company interviewers regarding this project architecture.

Keyword matching checks for exact string equality (e.g. searching for 'Node.js' misses 'NodeJS' or 'Express backend developer'). Semantic similarity converts words and sentences into high-dimensional vector embeddings, measuring conceptual proximity via cosine distance regardless of trivial spelling or phrasing variations.
